items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Buddy P.T., Sam Morgan, you know, they'd be bucking against one of them.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, you see, Shreveport, they never had no music for funerals around there at all, but they heard it by New Orleans. A lot of fellas coming down there and they'd see them funerals down there, you know, and some of them would remember. Well, they had a, he was a veteran from the Spanish-American War way back then. And it was his request to have some kind of music when you die, you know. So everybody knew I had been down this way, living down this way. They say, look, we got to have some kind of music at the…
Buddy P.T., Sam Morgan, you know, they'd be bucking against one of them. One right behind them, one band on a big truck or something like that.

After Rene A. They play the next fella playing the next on down. So we was out of town dudes. We was hung on the last truck behind. Free music. That was in 1914. That was in 1914. I remember it coming to me. Mm-hm. We'd be bucking against one another, one right behind her and one band on a big truck or something like that. After Rene played the next fella playing the next on down. So we was out of town dudes, we was hung on the last truck behind. Free music. That was in 1914. I remember it coming to me.
